text:
rachel: quick report - seeing a recurring goroutine leak in the go sample that does generator streaming + auth hotswap. filing notes before a PR.

rachel: repro (short): start generator.Stream(ctx, req), spin a goroutine that calls stream.SetBearer(token) on refresh, then cancel ctx after first chunk. caller returns but background goroutine sometimes stays ~20-40s. process shows goroutine stuck in SetBearer.

rachel: snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for t := range tokenC { iter.SetBearer(t) }
}()
_ = iter.Recv() // first chunk
cancel()
// main returns but SetBearer goroutine still alive sometimes
```

ben: the core issue is SetBearer doing blocking work (mutex + handshake) without honoring ctx. canceling ctx doesn't unblock that path.

kai: ergonomics goal: cancel == fast, deterministic teardown. options: (A) make SetBearer nonblocking (atomic token swap + notify send loop), (B) accept ctx on SetBearer so caller can cancel the handshake, (C) add a ForceClose/Abort that nukes transport immediately.

marie: +1 to nonblocking swap as the default safe behavior. Provide a separate Reauth(ctx) that performs the blocking handshake and returns an error if reauth fails. That keeps normal token refresh cheap.

ben: also propose StreamV2 that returns a StreamHandle with these methods: Recv(), Done() <-chan struct{}, Err() error, ForceClose() error, SetBearerFast(token). Done() closes once all internals cleaned up. Err() returns canonical terminal cause (context.Canceled / DeadlineExceeded / io.EOF / upstream error).

rachel: that would help onboarding examples. doc snippet: "If you need to interrupt a generator, cancel the ctx then wait on iter.Done() for cleanup. Use iter.ForceClose() only if you need immediate teardown."

kai: small implementation detail: when SetBearerFast swaps token, apply token at next chunk boundary to avoid header races. Use atomic.Value or mutex-free pointer swap + channel wake.

marie: tests: add examples/stream-hotswap that rotates tokens, cancels ctx, and asserts Done() closes within 100ms. Also add server fixture that delays handshake response so we can assert ForceClose aborts any blocked SetBearer/Reauth.

ops-bot: note: create a draft PR with prefix "devex/stream-hotswap" to auto-assign reviewers from devex + eng-runtime. Include CHANGELOG, tests, and onboarding doc snippet.

ben: compatibility: keep old Stream(...) API as a shim over StreamV2 for now to avoid semver surprises. Land StreamV2 behind feature flag if needed.

rachel: i'll prototype SetBearerFast + StreamHandle.Done + ForceClose. will add small example app and tests and post PR link here.

devrel-bot: quick reminder: please add a short code sample in the Getting Started guide showing the cancel pattern: cancel ctx, wait on iter.Done(), or call iter.ForceClose() if immediate shutdown required. PR labeled "docs/stream-cancel" will request docs review.

kai: one more UX note: normalize final error via iter.Err() so calling code can reliably tell if terminal cause was cancellation vs EOF. That avoids accidental retries on EOF when ctx was the cause.

marie: agreed. Err() should prefer context errors when ctx.Done() triggered first, even if transport later returns EOF. Use an atomic terminalError set-once.

rachel: thanks all  I'll open a draft with prototypes and examples. will ping runtime if ForceClose leaves kernel-level sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.
